service_answer.outcome.refused_at_submit: the service (or the MCP tool / SDK before it) refuses; no host request is made
service_answer.outcome.answered: the service answers what the host refuses, or reshapes the request (split, normalised, merged, mapped) before the host sees it
service_answer.outcome.clamped: the service sends a value the host would not use by default (a lower default, a held configured value), so the answer is computed under a different limit
service_answer.outcome.not_expressible: the MCP tool has no argument for it (missing_argument); extra tools/call arguments are silently dropped by the MCP SDK
service_answer.outcome.relayed: ADDED beyond the four requested: the request reaches the host (a job is created) and the host's own refusal comes back under a service code (text_contains is the stable part)

vocabulary.service_answer.stage: where the answer is decided: mcp_local (tool body, no REST call), fastmcp_args (MCP SDK argument validation/coercion), mcp_schema (no argument), rest_model (the REST pydantic model, mapped to 400 by the route class), rest_validator (app.pattern.validate), rest_planner (app.traversal planner/presets), route (the REST route), plan (the request the service builds), job (after the backend call)
vocabulary.service_answer.http: the HTTP status of the REST route behind the tool (the MCP result itself has none: compare error.code / error.field); null for mcp_local / fastmcp_args / answered
vocabulary.service_answer.text_contains: the stable part of the service's error text (contained in it). ADDED 2026-10-14 (triage-2 B-07): `a | b` lists alternatives, any one of which holds (each part stripped), as for code and field: pattern.predicate_form_other states one text per form fault

agreement.by_design: a mapped pair counts as agreement
agreement.not_implemented_mcp: the scenario is 'not implemented yet via MCP'

vocabulary.answer_match: ADDED 2026-10-13: an answer-triggered case: it applies to any scenario on one of `routes` whose MCP answer matches `mcp` (http, code, text_contains, field), whatever the scenario names; the comparator marks the pair verified when a direct execution of the scenario matches `direct`; a direct answer outside `direct` is read by `direct_mismatch` (ADDED 2026-10-14). Load validation (ADDED 2026-10-14, triage-2 B-08; the async runner's ServiceByDesign.problems refuses the table, naming the case): `routes` is required (a non-empty list of routes); answer_match states only routes, direct, mcp, direct_mismatch, wall_rule; a side only http, code, text_contains, field, slot_code; on the mcp side `http` is one integer, `slot_code` is not allowed (a direct-side key: a host 200 body's slot refusal) and `code` is required (ADDED 2026-10-14, peer review R5: an mcp side with only an http would make every answer on the route with that status by design); direct_mismatch is disagree or timing; wall_rule is budget_minus_reserve
vocabulary.answer_match.mcp.field: ADDED 2026-10-14 (optional): the refused argument's field (the MCP error's `field`) as a pattern: `<...>` placeholders match anything, `a | b` lists alternatives (each part stripped), matched like a named case's service_answer.field; an MCP answer that names no field does not match. It tells apart refusals of one code and text whose host answers differ (pattern.caps_zero: a cap of 0 the host answers, against time_budget_ms 0 with the same REST text, which the host refuses)
vocabulary.answer_match.direct.slot_code: ADDED 2026-10-14 (optional): a pattern slot's error code: the direct answer (a 200) holds a pattern whose slot is refused with it (body.patterns[].error.code; `a | b` lists alternatives), where the service refuses the whole submit (mismatch.above_kind_cap: the host's mismatches_above_cap slot)
vocabulary.answer_match.direct_mismatch: ADDED 2026-10-14 (triage-2 B-03; stated on every answer_match of the table; the comparator reads it, the MCP runner has no direct arm): what a direct answer outside answer_match.direct means for the pair. "disagree": any direct HTTP answer outside the direct side disagrees (pattern.caps_zero, mismatch.above_kind_cap, traverse.empty_seeds: validation or a stale cap, no timing involved). "timing": a direct 200 or a direct 503 deadline (code deadline) reads unverified, a timing difference (the same request, the host finished at another time); any other direct answer (e.g. a 4xx refusal) disagrees (pattern.deadline_ends_task). A direct transport error or a missing direct answer is always unverified, whatever the value. The MCP execution's own checks still count: a finding is never erased by the mark (see explains_checks)
vocabulary.answer_match.wall_rule: ADDED 2026-10-14 (optional; peer review R1, the design lead's threshold; judged on the MCP execution, its mcp_phases and raw calls): "budget_minus_reserve" = the answer-triggered case applies only when the MCP execution's service-side wall reaches the request's time_budget_ms less the finalisation reserve (the reserve the MCP answer's error text states, "finalisation reserve of <N> ms", else 250 ms: app/pattern/validate.py DEFAULT_FINALIZE_RESERVE_MS): the host sends its deadline at budget - reserve at the earliest, so a relayed deadline before it is no host deadline (a budget bug the case would hide). The wall, in order: mcp_phases.backend_ms (the service-measured backend call); for a pattern search, the deadline-ended task's HTTP try (its diagnostic log's last held-slot line, http 1 fail 1 <s>s: the failed POST's seconds, app/queue/held_span.py; the smallest over such tasks; a task without one, or with more than one try, gives none). The request's time_budget_ms is the MCP arguments' (else the direct request's). A KNOWN wall below the threshold: the case does not apply, matching continues with the other cases and, when none applies, the checks judge. CHANGED 2026-10-14 (rule (c), the design lead): no wall (no backend_ms, no usable slot line) or no threshold (no request budget): plausibility undecidable: the case matched (recorded) and the execution is inconclusive with verdict_detail "no service-side timing: plausibility undecidable" or "no threshold known: plausibility undecidable", never the checks' fail (a finding still wins). The line's verdict_detail says why. pattern.deadline_ends_task states it
vocabulary.direct_expectation.http: the host's HTTP status: an integer, or (ADDED 2026-10-14) a list of statuses any one of which holds, e.g. [200, 503] where the host accepts the request and may still overrun its budget (pattern.time_budget_below_minimum); null: not stated
vocabulary.direct_expectation.text_prefix: ADDED 2026-10-14 (optional): the host's error text starts with it, for a text whose tail varies with the request (resolve.unknown_label names the label); `text` is then null. Compared as is (no digit folding)
vocabulary.explains_checks: ADDED 2026-10-14 (triage-2 B-01; answered / clamped cases only, stated on each of them): the checks (checks.py names) whose failure the service's path explains. An entry is a check name (it explains every failure of that check) or (ADDED 2026-10-14, peer review R4) an object {"check": <name>, "detail_matches": <regex>}: it explains a failure of that check only when the check's detail matches the regex completely (Python re.fullmatch with re.S; checks.py joins several violations of one check with "; " into one detail, so a detail carrying another violation beside the explained one is not matched). Load validation: a list; an object states check (a non-empty name) and detail_matches (a regex that compiles) and no other key (traverse.duplicate_seeds explains only the merged-seed count message of invariants, "1 results for 2 seeds"). An answered or clamped match never decides before the checks: F = the execution's failing checks, E = F ∩ explains_checks, U = F - E; U non-empty -> fail; else r = checks.scenario_outcome over the checks without E: r finding -> finding, E non-empty -> service_by_design, else r. [] (or absent) explains nothing: the checks decide and the case is a note (the line records service_by_design_case and explained_checks = E). A refused, relayed or answer-triggered match stays service_by_design (the host never answered), except that any check that is a finding makes it finding: a by-design mark never erases a finding (e.g. a relayed deadline's budget_respected)

service_answer.detail: The service splits the patterns into chunks of the host's caps.max_patterns (16; 16 also when the host states none), one task (one host request) per chunk; every pattern is answered and get_status merges them per pattern. Each chunk is its own host request with the FULL time_budget_ms and the per-request caps (max_steps, max_predicate_work, ...), so per-request work and timing are not those of one request.
